content:
This commit "chore(RepresentationTheory): remove some set_option backwards" is tagged as v4.32.0-rc1-patch1.

I'm curious as to why -- is the change meaningful enough to be marked as such? Usually tags are associated with toolchain bumps.

Looking at the release, possibly a mistake by @Edison Xie ?

edit: Sorry, misunderstanding on my part!
I believe GitHub's UI always shows the commit author and implies they pushed the tag without any actual basis.
No idea why a tag like this would be pushed, but it wasn't me. Likely it was a mistake?
Hm, it seems to be used by https://github.com/kim-em/hex-dev, so I suspect it was created by @Kim Morrison
I don't understand why that project would not simply pin its dependency to a specific sha instead though?

The only other instances of these are

v4.14.0-patch1
v4.15.0-patch1

which seem to have been pushed by @Kim Morrison. But notably these are not part of the master history, whereas this 4.32.0-rc1-patch1is

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

Looking at the release, possibly a mistake by Edison Xie ?

edit: Sorry, misunderstanding on my part!

Phew :cold_sweat:

The v4.32.0-rc1 tag at Mathlib was defective (sorry, not immediately remembering how) because of the problem described at batteries#1868, so I made a tag later down Mathlib history. I didn't do it at the earliest possible moment, which might have been easier to decipher...
